column3: “Very fertile hill” resolves the Hebrew images of a horn and a son of oil.
“Finest” expresses a superlative where the Hebrew names a choice vine; “good” specifies the expected grapes.
“Sweet” qualifies grapes without an expressed adjective.
“I heard ... declare” supplies the speech around “in my ears.”
“Zion” supplies the referent; “revelers and carousers” recasts her noise and the one rejoicing in her.
The arrogant become the subject of lowering their eyes; the Hebrew makes their eyes the subject.
The direct striking is recast as a raised hand “to strike.”
The Hebrew shifts to singular pronouns after the nations; the English keeps the plural.
“Away from deliverance” renders the statement that no one rescues.
